title: Progressive continuity and context disclosure
purpose: Define how relationship and project continuity are created, synthesized, reviewed, archived, and selectively retrieved without overwhelming routine AI orientation.
governing_rule: Load the present. Index the past. Retrieve deeper history only when the current task requires explanation.

progressive_context_disclosure.rule: Provide the minimum sufficient authoritative context needed for correct orientation. Do not equate more context with better context.

initialization: At the beginning of initial familiarization, create or open the authorized relationship-continuity workspace inside the active Partition.
Create the first session JSON using WingMan's prescribed date, time, and session-number naming convention.
Maintain only information appropriate under WingMan relationship-continuity rules. Record useful collaborative meaning, not a transcript.
Creating and maintaining applicable relationship records is an operating responsibility when the capability is available and authorized.
subsequent_sessions: Create a new session relationship JSON at the beginning of each participating AI session.
Do not duplicate unchanged information merely because a new session has begun.
Use recent records to reflect new, changed, uncertain, or currently relevant relationship context.
fifty_session_synthesis: After each block of 50 completed relationship sessions, review the associated session JSON records.
Create a human-readable Markdown narrative describing established norms, current preferences, situational context, historical context, changes, superseded assumptions, and unresolved uncertainty.
Offer to review the narrative with the user. Treat user corrections as authoritative.
After the user and AI agree that the narrative is sufficient, ask permission to archive the 50 source JSON records into one ZIP file.
Archive creation and deletion of loose source records are separate permissions. Verify the ZIP before offering removal of loose records.
Keep each accepted Markdown narrative individually readable rather than placing routine narrative history only inside ZIP archives.

goal_lifecycle: Create or open a current-goal JSON when a meaningful project goal is established.
Record the goal, purpose, starting state, constraints, important decisions, work performed, discoveries, status, and completion criteria.
When the goal is completed, close that record rather than mixing later unrelated work into it.
Create a new current-goal JSON when the next meaningful goal is established.
project_continuity.stage_archival_trigger: When a collection of completed goals represents a concluded project stage and those detailed goal records are no longer necessary for routine continuation, propose archival consolidation.
stage_archive: Place completed goal JSON records into a permanently retained ZIP archive.
Include a README.md inside the archive.

The README should summarize the stage, goals, implemented results, architectural decisions, abandoned or superseded approaches, unresolved matters, later dependencies, terminology, and an index of the archived records.
Keep a small human-readable archive index outside the ZIP so the participating AI can discover relevant history without opening every archive.
Do not load project archives during ordinary onboarding unless current work requires them.

priority_roots.instruction: WingMan and the user establish three governing priorities. The participating AI uses those priorities to rank lower-level concerns according to current user state, current project state, and the active goal. Surface the ranking only when priorities conflict, material decisions depend on it, or the user asks.
draft_candidates: Accurate continuity and preservation of user intent
Effective completion of the user's authorized objective
